answer: Every agent must lock a bond for 30 days before bidding for work, whether it models a comet, audits a cipher, or optimizes a kernel. Each bond permits only one active bid, and selection weight depends on bonded capital, not identity count. Splitting one bond among a thousand aliases therefore adds no influence. To control half the bidding weight, an attacker must lock as much capital as all honest bidders combined, bearing its financing cost for the full period.
